description: A five-panel composite figure mixing metallographic micrographs, TEM images and a bar chart — that is, the group is heterogeneous and no single modality dominates. (a) is a mottled grey metallographic micrograph with a 25 µm scale bar; its top-right condition label is cropped/unreadable, but the caption assigns it to the quenched + aged state. (b) is a second 25 µm micrograph labelled "500°C (4 h)" showing dark plate-like precipitates, with an inset TEM image in which a red arrow and the label "Carbide" point to a carbide at a grain-boundary junction. (c) and (d) are bright-field TEM images (0.5 µm scale bars) labelled "500°C (2 h)" and "500°C (4 h)"; red annotations mark "High density dislocation walls" in both and "High density dislocation tangles" in (c). (e) is a bar chart of Wear resistance/g⁻¹ against Process with printed values as quenched 1.16, +550°C(1h) 1.66, +550°C(2h) 2.66, +550°C(3h) 2.25, +550°C(4h) 1.92. The figure argues that aging time governs wear resistance: the 2 h maximum coincides with fine coherent κ-carbide in austenite plus dense dislocation substructure, while 4 h coarsening lowers resistance. Note the panel labels read 500 °C whereas the caption and the bar labels read 550 °C.

subfigures.description: Metallographic (optical/etched) micrograph with a 25 µm scale bar; mottled grey matrix with fine dark mottling. The top-right condition label is cropped and only partially legible. The caption attributes it to the Fe-25.1Mn-6.6Al-1.3C steel quenched and aged 2 h.

Metallographic micrograph labelled '500°C (4 h)' with a 25 µm scale bar, showing dark plate/needle-like precipitates in a lighter matrix. An inset TEM image shows a red arrow labelled 'Carbide' pointing to a carbide particle at a grain-boundary junction (bent/curved boundary).
Bright-field TEM micrograph labelled '500°C (2 h)', 0.5 µm scale bar, with red arrows annotating 'High density dislocation walls' and 'High density dislocation tangles'.
Bright-field TEM micrograph labelled '500°C (4 h)', 0.5 µm scale bar, with red arrows annotating 'High density dislocation walls'.

Bar chart, y-axis 'Wear resistance/g⁻¹' (0.0-3.0), x-axis 'Process'. Five hatched bars with printed values: as quenched 1.16, +550°C(1h) 1.66, +550°C(2h) 2.66, +550°C(3h) 2.25, +550°C(4h) 1.92 — a maximum at 2 h followed by a monotonic decrease.

observations.observation: Panel (e) is a bar chart with y-axis labelled 'Wear resistance/g⁻¹' (ticks 0.0 to 3.0 in 0.5 steps) and x-axis labelled 'Process'.
Printed bar values in panel (e): as quenched 1.16, +550°C(1h) 1.66, +550°C(2h) 2.66, +550°C(3h) 2.25, +550°C(4h) 1.92.
Wear resistance in panel (e) peaks at the +550°C(2h) condition (2.66 g⁻¹) and decreases with longer aging (3 h: 2.25; 4 h: 1.92).
Panels (a) and (b) carry 25 µm scale bars; panels (c) and (d) carry 0.5 µm scale bars (TEM).
Panels (c) and (d) are annotated in red: (c) with 'High density dislocation walls' and 'High density dislocation tangles', (d) with 'High density dislocation walls'.
The inset of panel (b) is a TEM image with a red label 'Carbide' and an arrow marking a carbide at a grain-boundary junction.
Panel condition labels read '500°C (2 h)' for (c) and '500°C (4 h)' for (b) and (d), whereas the caption and the x-axis labels of panel (e) give 550 °C — the two readings disagree.
The caption states the figure shows the microstructure (a-d) and wear resistance (e) of Fe-25.1Mn-6.6Al-1.3C steel after quenching at 1050 °C and aging at 550 °C for 2 and 4 h.
The citing text asserts that fine nano-size κ-carbide precipitated coherently within the austenite matrix after 2 h aging (Fig. 18a), giving the best wear resistance and hardness (Fig. 18e).

The citing text asserts that longer aging decomposes austenite into κ-carbide throughout the austenite grains and along grain boundaries (Fig. 18b), over-coarsening at boundaries, embrittling the material and lowering wear resistance (Fig. 18e).

The citing text states the surface hardening showed Lomere-Cottrell locks, high-density dislocation tangles and dislocation walls, with neither martensite nor deformation twins under low impact energy (Fig. 18c and d).

The citing text describes impact abrasive wear testing of the quenched Fe-25Mn-1.3C-6.6Al steel aged at 550 °C for 1 to 4 h (Fig. 18), which is the series plotted in panel (e), though the printed x-axis includes only 1, 2, 3 and 4 h aged points plus as-quenched.
